patch.summary: Is SaneBox worth it? SaneBox is inbox-productivity tooling that layers onto an existing mailbox — Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, iCloud or any IMAP account — and triages incoming mail into folders such as SaneLater, SaneBlackHole and SaneAttachments, with follow-up reminders on higher tie…. Strong when Individuals and small teams drowning in inbound email who want automatic triage. Weak when Not a communication channel — SaneBox triages an existing mailbox and adds no voice, SMS, WhatsApp or chat.

scenarios.title: Limitations that change the deal
scenarios.body: Not a communication channel — SaneBox triages an existing mailbox and adds no voice, SMS, WhatsApp or chat; Billing is per person with no team or family plan, so multi-user rollouts multiply cost; Mailbox caps drive upgrades: 1 account on Snack, 2 on Lunch, 4 on Dinner

Counter-signal: Walk when Not a communication channel — SaneBox triages an existing mailbox and adds no voice, SMS, WhatsApp or chat would block go-live.

Capability hinge for this product: analytics and reporting; AI assistance; unified inbox.

Integrations in research: Gmail, Outlook, Icloud.

Paid tiers that usually matter in evaluation: Snack, Lunch, Dinner.

sections.heading: Who SaneBox is worth it for — and who should avoid it
sections.body:
Worth it for: Choose SaneBox when the problem is inbound email volume on mailboxes you already have — and treat it as adjacent to, not part of, your business communications stack..

Avoid if: For business communications proper, compare Aircall, CallHippo, KrispCall or Freshcaller for voice, Wati for WhatsApp, and Zenzap for team chat; consider Fastmail if you want to replace the mailbox itself..

If avoid signals dominate, start the alternative path with Fastmail on the same job-to-be-done.

sections.heading: SaneBox price/value and next evaluation step
sections.body:
Prove one real workflow on the documented free/trial path before arguing for Snack.

Next step: run analytics and reporting end-to-end, then decide.
